summary: Fix for 554/555: the owner-authorization state functions (owner_authorization_sent, owner_authorization_record, owner_authorization_mark_executed, conversion_decide_object_delegated) run as SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, because the server role has only SELECT/INSERT on owner_authorizations and the first request failed at owner_authorization_sent after its email was sent. The one request left without its email identity (it can never be authorized) is revoked with the reason kept. No other row changes.

preflight.name: no owner authorization has been authorized or executed
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM owner_authorizations WHERE status IN ('authorized', 'executed')

preflight.name: at most one request was sent without its email identity (the failed 7C1D2880 request)
preflight.sql: SELECT (count(*) <= 1)::int FROM owner_authorizations WHERE status = 'requested' AND request_message_id IS NULL

expected_changes: The four owner-authorization state functions become SECURITY DEFINER with search_path = public; service_role keeps only SELECT/INSERT on owner_authorizations.
The request sent without its email identity is revoked (reason kept in execution); nothing else changes.

verify.name: the four state functions are SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path
verify.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_proc WHERE proname IN ('owner_authorization_sent', 'owner_authorization_record', 'owner_authorization_mark_executed', 'conversion_decide_object_delegated') AND prosecdef AND array_to_string(proconfig, ',') LIKE '%search_path=public%'

verify.name: no open request lacks its email identity
verify.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM owner_authorizations WHERE status = 'requested' AND request_message_id IS NULL

verify.name: the server role still cannot UPDATE the table directly
